question: What incentive values does the SuSI Program's ADI offer for net metered non-residential projects located on rooftops, carports, canopies, and floating solar in New Jersey?
gold_answers: The ADI Program offers $110 per SREC-II for net metered non-residential projects smaller than 1 MW and $100 per SREC-II for projects between 1 MW and 5 MW. Public entities can receive an additional $20 adder, making it $130 per SREC-II for smaller projects and $120 per SREC-II for larger ones.

gold_answers: If, in a monthly billing period, the billing credit associated with the Subscription of a Low-Income Subscriber exceeds the Subscriber's bill from the Utility, the excess billing credit will be rolled over as a dollar amount bill credit from month to month indefinitely until the Subscriber terminates service with the Utility at which time no payment shall be made by the Utility for any remaining bill credits associated with the Low-Income Subscriber's Subscription.

question: What does the City of Sacramento require for newly constructed buildings in terms of all-electric building requirements?
gold_answers:
All newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings if permit applications are filed on or after January 1, 2023.
**Context** - For building permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, except as provided in subsections 101.12.6 and 101.12.7, all newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings.

### QA Pair 2
**Question** - When does the requirement for all newly constructed buildings to be all-electric become mandatory in Sacramento?
**Answer** - The requirement becomes mandatory for buildings with permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023.
**Context** - For building permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, except as provided in subsections 101.12.6 and 101.12.7, all newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings.

### QA Pair 3
**Question** - What exemptions are available for constructing mixed fuel buildings under the City of Sacramento's policy?
**Answer** - Limited exemptions include ground floor food service establishments for areas with cooking equipment, manufacturing or industrial facilities with process loads, and water-heating systems in regulated affordable housing where virtual net energy metering is unavailable.
**Context** - Limited exemptions for building permit applications filed on or before December 31, 2025, include ground floor food service establishments, manufacturing or industrial facilities, and regulated affordable housing.

### QA Pair 4
**Question** - When does the exemption for limited sectors end in relation to the all-electric building requirements in Sacramento?
**Answer** - The exemptions for limited sectors such as ground floor food service establishments, manufacturing or industrial facilities, and regulated affordable housing end on January 1, 2026.
**Context** - The section 101.12.1 and section 101.12.2 requirements to construct all-electric buildings shall not apply to sectors with limited exemptions until January 1, 2026

answer_facts: Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: # Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive ***created_at*** : 2021-10-01 00:00:00 ***updated_at*** : 2023-12-15 15:57:01 ***state** : New Jersey **implementing sector***: State ***program category*** : Financial Incentive ***program type*** : Performance-Based Incentive ***sector*** : Commercial, Industrial, Local Government, Nonprofit, Residential, Schools, State Government, Agricultural, Multifamily Residential, Low Income Residential, Institutional ***start date*** : 2021-08-28 04:00:00 ***administrator*** : Board of Public Utilities ***Incentive Amount*** : Net-Metered Residential: $85/SREC-II Small Net-Metered Non-Residential located on Rooftop, Carport, Canopy and Floating Solar Projects smaller than 1 MW (dc): $110/SREC-II, $130 for public entities Projects 1 MW to 5 MW (dc): $100/SREC-II, $120 for public entities Net Metered Non-Residential Ground Mount Projects smaller than 1 MW (dc): $90/SREC-II, $110 for public entities Projects 1 MW to 5 MW (dc): $85/SREC-II, $105 for public entities Community Solar Permanent Program (LMI only): $90/SREC-II Interim Subsection (t) Grid: $100/SREC-II Subsection (t) applies to facilities located on brownfield, properly closed landfill, or historic fill sites.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: Current available capacity is posted on the homepage of the [ADI online portal.](https://njadi.programprocessing.com/) **Market Segment** | **System Size (MW-DC)** | **Incentive Values ($/SREC-II)** | **Public Entities ($20 Adder)** ---|---|---|--- Net-Metered Residential | All Sizes | $85 | N/A Net-Metered Non-Residential located on rooftop, carport, canopy, and floating solar | Smaller than 1 MW 1 MW - 5 MW | $110 $100 | $130 $120 Net-Metered Non-Residential ground mount | Smaller than 1 MW 1 MW - 5 MW | $90 $85 | $105 $105 Community Solar LMI | Up to 5 MW | $90 | N/A Community Solar Non-LMI (Removed) | Up to 5 MW | LMI Only | N/A Interim Subsection (t) Grid | All Sizes | $100 | N/A An additional $20 adder is available for a public entity, a customer that is a State entity, school district, county, county agency, county authority, municipality, municipal agency, municipal authority, New Jersey public college, or New Jersey public university.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: A [Board Order](https://nj.gov/bpu/agenda/2023calendar/approved/20230308.html) from March 6, 2023 revised the ADI SREC-II values, effective March 13, 2023.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: ***Maximum Incentive*** : MW-DC Capacity Blocks Net Metered Residential: 250 MW Net Metered Non-Residential: 257 MW Community Solar Program: 225 MW ***Eligible System Size*** : Net Metered Residential: All sizes Net Metered Non-Residential: 5 MW-DC max Community Solar Program: 5 MW-DC max ***Equipment Requirements*** : All solar equipment must be new ## Summary : By [Board Order](https://www.njcleanenergy.com/files/file/TI%20Program/FY22/8A%20ORDER%20Successor%20Solar%20Incentive.pdf) on July 28, 2021, the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) established the SuSI Program to implement the Clean Energy Act of 2018 (L. 2018, c.17) and the Solar Act of 2021 (L. 2021, c. 169).

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: **[Competitive Solar Incentive Program](https://njcleanenergy.com/renewable- energy/programs/susi-program/csi-program)** This program provides competitively set incentives, as bid by developers, for non-residential projects with nameplate capacity over 5 MW.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The interim market segment is blocked for 75 MW, while net-metered residential, net- metered non-residential, and community solar (The [permanent CS program](https://njcleanenergy.com/renewable-energy/programs/susi- program/csep) rules from October 2023 require all CS systems to meet 51% LMI participation and removed the non-LMI incentive) is blocked for 225 MW in energy years 2024 and 2025.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The SuSI Program is made up of two sub-programs: **[Administratively Determined Incentive Program](https://njcleanenergy.com/renewable-energy/programs/susi-program/adi- program)** The ADI Program provides incentives for net metered residential projects, net metered non-residential projects of 5 MW or less, all community solar projects, and, for an interim period, projects previously eligible to seek conditional certification from the Board under Subsection (t).

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: See the [Competitive Solar Incentive Program](https://programs.dsireusa.org/system/program/detail/22480/) description in DSIRE for more information.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The SuSI Program replaces the SREC Registration Program (SRP), which was closed to new registration on April 30, 2020 pursuant to the Clean Energy Act, and the Transition Incentive (TI) Program, which provided a bridge between the Legacy SRP and the SuSI Program.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The program will accept new registrations for each market segment on a first-come, first-served basis until the block is fully subscribed.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The Interim Subsection is available on an interim basis for solar facilities certified as being located on brownfield, historic fill, or properly closed landfills.

question: In Rhode Island, under the Offshore Wind Energy Target, can developers of newly developed offshore wind energy resources pay construction employees wages and benefits less than the prevailing wage and fringe benefit rates at the journeyman level if the employee is a participant in an approved apprenticeship program?
gold_answers: No

selected.title: § 39-31-10. Offshore wind procurement.
selected.text: (f) Developers of newly developed renewable energy resources shall pay each construction, operations and maintenance employees wages and benefits that are not less than the prevailing wage and fringe benefit rates at the journeyman level that are prescribed by the department of labor and training pursuant to chapter 13 of title 37, for the corresponding classification in which the employee is employed, and not less than the prevailing wage rates for employees for which there is no classification prescribed by the department of labor and training; provided that, a worker may be paid wages and benefits not less than the rate applicable to apprentices for the pertinent classification if: (1) The worker is a participant in an approved apprenticeship program; and (2) The approved apprenticeship program from which the apprentice is hired maintains a direct entry agreement with a certified pre-apprenticeship training program.

question: As a commercial business owner in Iowa, how does the Energy Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program evaluate projects for approval, and what specific criteria must be met to be considered for a loan exceeding $1 million?
gold_answers: The program evaluates projects based on whether they demonstrate broad reaching benefits to the state, local community, or utility ratepayers, a creative or innovative approach to a need or problem, or if assistance is necessary to reduce the project's risks. Applicants requesting a loan over $1 million must, at a minimum, demonstrate that the project offers broad reaching benefits.

question: As a farmer in California, what is my legal obligation when installing a variable speed drive (VSD) for an agricultural process fan to be eligible for the PG&E GoGreen Business Energy Financing rebate?
gold_answers: To install an Agricultural Process Fan VSD, the fan must not be used for HVAC, exhaust, pressurization or other process applications. The individual fan motors must not exceed 5 horsepower (hp), and the fan must operate continuously or be manually operated with an ON/OFF control switch. Additionally, the fan motors must not be two-speed or have an existing VSD, and the VSD must control multiple fans up to 5 hp each in arrays with one VSD or with one VSD for each fan. The VSD must vary the speed of the fan automatically based on ambient conditions, and the rebate is applicable only to agricultural buildings in certain climate zones (CZ06, CZ07, CZ08, CZ09, CZ10, CZ11, CZ12, CZ13, CZ14, and CZ15).

question: How is Illinois Solar for All Program funded?
gold_answers:
The Illinois Solar for All Program has a budget of $66,500,000 annually.
**Context** - ***budget*** : $66,500,000 annually

### QA Pair 4
**Question** - What are the different sub-programs under the Illinois Solar for All Program?
**Answer** - The four sub-programs under the Illinois Solar for All Program are: the Low-Income Single-Family and Small Multifamily Solar Incentive (also referred to as "Residential Solar (Small)"); the Low-Income Community Solar Project Initiative (referred to as "Community Solar"); the Non-Profit and Public Facilities program; and the Low-Income Multifamily Solar Incentive (referred to as "Residential Solar (Large)** "** ).
**Context** - The Illinois Solar for All Program consists of four sub-programs: the **Low-Income Single-Family and Small Multifamily Solar Incentive** (also referred to as "**Residential Solar (Small)** "); the **Low-Income Community Solar Project Initiative** (referred to as "**Community Solar** "); the **Non-Profit and Public Facilities** program; and the **Low-Income****Multifamily Solar Incentive** (referred to as "**Residential Solar (Large)** ").

### QA Pair 5
**Question** - What is the eligibility criteria for the Illinois Solar for All Program?
**Answer** - The Illinois Solar for All Program targets low-income residents, non-profit and public facilities to participate in solar projects by offering more generous REC prices than the Illinois Shines program.
**Context** - By offering more generous REC prices than the [Illinois Shines](https://programs.dsireusa.org/system/program/detail/22441/adjustable-block-program-illinois-shines) program, the Illinois Solar for All program incents low-income residents (as well as non-profit and public facilities) to participate in solar projects, whether as a system owner, community solar project subscriber, or system host.

### QA Pair 6
**Question** - What is the duration of enrollment for the Bright Neighborhoods Initiative under the Illinois Solar for All Program?
**Answer** - The enrollment for the Bright Neighborhoods Initiative was open through March 31, 2024.
**Context** - Enrollment was open through March 31, 2024.

### QA Pair 7
**Question** - What changes are recommended for the re-launch of the Bright Neighborhoods initiative under the Illinois Solar for All Program?
**Answer** - The Illinois Solar for All is recommending design changes for a re-launch of the Bright Neighborhoods initiative for the new program year.
**Context** - Illinois Solar for All is recommending design changes for a re-launch of the Bright Neighborhoods initiative for the new program year

gold_answers: The Residential Demand Response Battery Incentive Program is a policy from Entergy Mississippi that offers a one-time $2,000 cash incentive to any retail residential customer with an eligible DGIC (distributed generation interconnection customer) who installs a battery storage system with a minimum storage capacity of 8 kWh and enrolls in the Company's Battery Demand Response program. The customer must certify that the battery complies with the company's Battery Demand Response Program. This incentive is available on a first-come, first-served basis until the end of 2027.

question: What are the conditions for residential customers to be eligible for Madison Gas & Electric's Charge Ahead Program?
gold_answers: To be eligible for the Charge Ahead Program, residential customers only need to charge their electric vehicles primarily during off-peak hours, with no requirement for having their own charging station. The program offers a credit of $8 per month during the summer and $4 per month during other months when customers charge at least 80% off-peak.

gold_answers: The purposes include: (1) acquisition and installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure, (2) proper operation and maintenance of electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and (3) data sharing about electric vehicle charging infrastructure to ensure long-term success of investments.

question: What is the method for determining the fair cash value of commercial solar energy system improvements in counties with fewer than 3,000,000 inhabitants under the Improvement Valuation of Commercial Solar Energy Systems policy?
gold_answers:
The fair cash value is determined by subtracting the allowance for physical depreciation from the trended real property cost basis.
**Context** - (35 ILCS 200/10-725 new)  
Sec. 10-725. Improvement valuation of commercial solar energy systems in counties with fewer than 3,000,000 inhabitants. Beginning in assessment year 2018, the fair cash value of commercial solar energy system improvements in counties with fewer than 3,000,000 inhabitants shall be determined by subtracting the allowance for physical depreciation from the trended real property cost basis.

### QA Pair number 2
**Question** - Are commercial solar energy systems assessable under this Division subject to equalization factors applied by the Department or any board of review, assessor, or chief county assessment officer?
**Answer** - No.
**Context** - (35 ILCS 200/10-735 new) Sec. 10-735. Commercial solar energy systems not subject to equalization. Commercial solar energy systems assessable under this Division are not subject to equalization factors applied by the Department or any board of review, assessor, or chief county assessment officer.

### QA Pair number 3
**Question** - What does the owner of a ground installed commercial solar energy system need to do upon commissioning a metes and bounds survey description of the land?
**Answer** - The owner shall deliver a copy of the survey to the chief county assessment officer and to the owner of the land upon which the ground installed commercial solar energy system is constructed.
**Context** - (35 ILCS 200/10-740 new)  
Sec. 10-740. Survey for ground installed commercial solar energy systems; parcel identification numbers for property improved with a ground installed commercial solar energy system. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the owner of the ground installed commercial solar energy system shall commission a metes and bounds survey description of the land upon which the commercial solar energy system is installed, including access routes, over which the owner of the commercial solar energy system has exclusive control.

### QA Pair number 4
**Question** - Who is liable for real estate taxes for the land and real property improvements of a ground-installed commercial solar energy system?
**Answer** - The owner of the commercial solar energy system is liable.
**Context** - # (35 ILCS 200/10-745 new)  
Sec. 10-745. Real estate taxes. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 9-175 of this Code, the owner of the commercial solar energy system shall be liable for the real estate taxes for the land and real property improvements of a ground installed commercial solar energy system

question: As a low-income residential customer participating in Entergy Mississippi's Residential Demand Response Battery Incentive Program with a Distributed Generation Facility (DGF), how is my bill calculated, and what happens to my excess energy credits?
gold_answers: Your monthly bill will be the total of any charges for usage as recorded on meter Channel 1, minus any credit due to you from excess energy exported to the Company as recorded on meter Channel 2. However, your excess energy credits will not be applied to reduce any fixed monthly customer charges or minimum bill provisions. Any remaining excess energy bill credit at the end of your service period will be issued to you as a check.
prediction: Based on the facts, your bill is calculated by applying the VDER rate, and any excess energy credits are used to offset your utility bill.

question: I am an Investor-Owned Utility in Michigan, and I want to understand how the state defines 'modified net metering' in the context of distributed generation. Can you explain the specifics of this billing method and how it impacts customer charges?
gold_answers: Modified net metering applies the power supply component of the full retail rate to the net of the bidirectional flow of kilowatt hours. Standby charges for customers on an energy rate schedule are equal to the retail distribution charge applied to the imputed customer usage during the billing period, which is calculated as the sum of the metered on-site generation and the net power flow.

answer_facts: Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: ***Maximum Incentive*** : MW-DC Capacity Blocks Net Metered Residential: 250 MW Net Metered Non-Residential: 257 MW Community Solar Program: 225 MW ***Eligible System Size*** : Net Metered Residential: All sizes Net Metered Non-Residential: 5 MW-DC max Community Solar Program: 5 MW-DC max ***Equipment Requirements*** : All solar equipment must be new ## Summary : By [Board Order](https://www.njcleanenergy.com/files/file/TI%20Program/FY22/8A%20ORDER%20Successor%20Solar%20Incentive.pdf) on July 28, 2021, the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) established the SuSI Program to implement the Clean Energy Act of 2018 (L. 2018, c.17) and the Solar Act of 2021 (L. 2021, c. 169).

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The interim market segment is blocked for 75 MW, while net-metered residential, net- metered non-residential, and community solar (The [permanent CS program](https://njcleanenergy.com/renewable-energy/programs/susi- program/csep) rules from October 2023 require all CS systems to meet 51% LMI participation and removed the non-LMI incentive) is blocked for 225 MW in energy years 2024 and 2025.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: Current available capacity is posted on the homepage of the [ADI online portal.](https://njadi.programprocessing.com/) **Market Segment** | **System Size (MW-DC)** | **Incentive Values ($/SREC-II)** | **Public Entities ($20 Adder)** ---|---|---|--- Net-Metered Residential | All Sizes | $85 | N/A Net-Metered Non-Residential located on rooftop, carport, canopy, and floating solar | Smaller than 1 MW 1 MW - 5 MW | $110 $100 | $130 $120 Net-Metered Non-Residential ground mount | Smaller than 1 MW 1 MW - 5 MW | $90 $85 | $105 $105 Community Solar LMI | Up to 5 MW | $90 | N/A Community Solar Non-LMI (Removed) | Up to 5 MW | LMI Only | N/A Interim Subsection (t) Grid | All Sizes | $100 | N/A An additional $20 adder is available for a public entity, a customer that is a State entity, school district, county, county agency, county authority, municipality, municipal agency, municipal authority, New Jersey public college, or New Jersey public university.

Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive: The SuSI Program is made up of two sub-programs: **[Administratively Determined Incentive Program](https://njcleanenergy.com/renewable-energy/programs/susi-program/adi- program)** The ADI Program provides incentives for net metered residential projects, net metered non-residential projects of 5 MW or less, all community solar projects, and, for an interim period, projects previously eligible to seek conditional certification from the Board under Subsection (t).

question: Can you explain the process outlined in Nevada Appliance and Equipment Energy Efficiency Standards for establishing and enforcing energy efficiency standards for appliances sold within the state?
gold_answers: The Director of the Office of Energy is required to adopt regulations establishing minimum standards of energy efficiency for certain appliances sold in the state and methods for verifying compliance. Sale, lease, rental, or installation of appliances not meeting these standards is prohibited after certain dates. The Director can also adopt standards for other appliances with specific findings, and manufacturers must submit certifications demonstrating compliance, including a mark, label, or tag identifying certified appliances.

selected.title: Utah - National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Grant Program
selected.text: With some limited exceptions, EV charging stations funded through the NEVI program should be spaced 50 miles apart and within one mile of the Interstate exit or highway._** The Utah Department of Transportation’s (UDOT) [NEVI plan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14_75QZLWVUaM-zmfB5N5MjqkA_SfUwwT/view) includes achieving build out status along the state's AFCs including I-15, I-70, I-80, I-84, I-215, and portions of US-6 and US-191.The state also plans to identify and begin building high-priority corridors that provide access to Utah’s five National Parks, forty-two State Parks, and other places of interest.

selected.title: Offshore Wind Energy Target
selected.text: The statutes provide additional details regarding the nature of the RFP and resulting contracts.

selected.title: § 39-31-10. Offshore wind procurement.
selected.text: The electric distribution company shall develop the request for proposals (RFP) in consultation with the Rhode Island office of energy resources and the Rhode Island division of public utilities and carriers.

selected.title: Offshore Wind Energy Target
selected.text: The deadline was later [amended](https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi- bin/legp604.exe?231+ful+CHAP0809) to December 31, 2032.

selected.title: § 39-31-10. Offshore wind procurement.
selected.text: The request for proposals shall require all bidders to provide, at a minimum, information on potential environmental impacts through the submittal of an environmental and fisheries mitigation plan, which shall include site and environmental data transparency requirements; a site layout plan and maps that illustrate the location of all onshore and offshore equipment and facilities and clearly delineates the perimeter of the area in which offshore wind turbines will be placed; annualized estimates for all economic benefits, including the specific in-state expenditures and employment proposed during the development, construction, and operation and maintenance phases of the project; a diversity, equity, and inclusion plan that, at a minimum, provides the bidder’s proposed strategy to enable access to employment and vendor opportunities for historically marginalized communities; identification of Rhode Island vendors and other domestic offshore wind supply chain opportunities associated with the project; and a plan outlining the bidder’s intentions with respect to the negotiation of a project labor agreement(s) to cover construction activities on a proposed project.

selected.title: § 39-31-10. Offshore wind procurement.
selected.text: This information shall be incorporated in the procurement’s evaluation and scoring criteria.
